title: heartbeat-response
description: The server's answer to a heartbeat: its time, the settings the agent's background monitors use, and, when this cabinet is in the current batch of a running rollout, the agent version it may upgrade to. Data only; the server can never send a command this way, and an offered upgrade is installed only if it passes every check against keys the server never holds.

hardwareIds.description: The scanner's hardware IDs from the console: the cabinet's own, else its site's, else its client's, else the fleet default. Whole IDs or vendor prefixes (USB\\VID_1234). null when none is set anywhere: the agent then finds the scanner itself by its Biometric device class.

upgrade.description: An agent release this cabinet is offered. The agent downloads it and the broker verifies it (docs/spec/07-upgrade-channel.md); the agent ignores an offer that is not newer than itself.

watchedServices.description: The services this cabinet must keep running: the cabinet's own list, else its site's, else its client's, else the fleet's (docs/spec/12-milestones-8-to-12.md). Empty when none is set.

approvedApps.description: The programs this cabinet may be asked to start, stop or restart: the cabinet's own list, else its site's, else its client's, else the fleet's. Empty when none is set. The agent keeps its own copy and acts only on these, re-checking the program it finds at the entry's exact path. Absent from an older server's answer, which leaves the agent with an empty list.

signed.description: The same list as an Admin signed it (docs/spec/09-open-decisions.md "Signing the approved list"): base64 of the signed document's exact bytes and the detached signature over them. An agent built with a list-signing key acts only on this, and only once the signature verifies; entries is kept for agents built before signing. Sent only to agents from 0.3.0 on, since an older agent refuses a field it does not know.

document.description: Base64 of the document's exact bytes (at most 32 KB).

intervals.description: Server-directed pacing. The server raises these under load or for cabinets on poor links; the agent clamps them to the given ranges and uses its defaults when absent.

heartbeatSeconds.description: Seconds between heartbeats (presence also comes from the long poll).

pollSeconds.description: How long a long poll is held.

eventsPaceMs.description: Pause between event batches while draining a backlog.
